$comment: Preregistration for #1567 (ageing policy) with the fixed reference time of #1568. Written BEFORE the runs. The policy itself is the owner's decision of 16.11.2026; this measurement does not decide it, it records what the switch does. The results are added in a separate `results` block under registration_version 2, never by editing this protocol.

arms.before: pre-#1567 policy: every staleness status at the explicit factors fresh 1.0 / aging 0.85 / stale 0.5 / expired 0.2, rules age like any note. Measurement variant of search-staleness.ts that differs from `after` only in `multiplierFor`.
arms.after: #1567 policy as shipped in search-staleness.ts: type-default ageing fresh 1.0 / aging 0.85 / stale 0.7 / expired 0.7; a note with a rulebook declaration (always / on-demand) gets no type-default ageing; an explicit valid_until or expires_after_days keeps the explicit factors.

protocol.path: production SearchIndex.recallHybrid, k 10, score floor 30, default RRF vector weight, local embeddinggemma via Ollama
protocol.reference_time: 2026-11-15T00:00:00.000Z (GOLDSET_REFERENCE_TIME, #1568) for the primary numbers; each run also reports `today` at its own wall clock
protocol.vault: copy of a real vault taken 2026-11-15 (~/.codex/worktrees/_vault-kopie-2026-11-15), copied again into a scratch directory so the run can write its own state; the original copy and the live vault are only read
protocol.dataset: the 12 gold files of v1-baseline.json (dataset sha256 69e1475010c64a0a02eee0b2fbc6929f3a33de1029ffc14eea36b91316dced00), minus every case whose expected or acceptable id is not in the vault copy. Rule fixed before the run; it removes 7 answerable cases (3 ids no longer exist), leaving 577 answerable, 79 no-answer, 36 probes — the population of the 15.11.2026 measurement
protocol.gate_flag: --gate (evidence decision, hook path) on both arms
protocol.code: git eba66497 plus the working-tree files of this change; their sha256 is recorded with the results
protocol.primary: strict R@3 on the 577 answerable cases, before vs after, at the reference time
secondary: R@1, R@10, MRR on the answerable cases
no-answer cases whose top served score is >= 100 (the replay of 15.11.2026 saw 35 -> 43 of 79)
per-case gains and losses at R@3 and R@10
protocol.expectation_from_replay: replay of 15.11.2026 on frozen candidate lists: R@3 170 -> 257 of 577, R@10 -> 324 of 577. Not a threshold; a large gap to it is a finding to explain
protocol.latency: micro-benchmark of applyStaleness on the vault copy (all notes as one hit pool), before vs after, 7 repeats; the after median must not exceed the before median by more than 5 %
protocol.longmemeval: LongMemEval notes are all type `reference` without an explicit deadline, so neither branch of the policy can fire there; recorded as a functional-identity check (count of notes the policy can touch), not as a second run
protocol.gate: descriptive. No threshold decides the switch; the owner decided it on 16.11.2026. The review of 40 to 60 lifted notes is separate and not replaced by these numbers.

$comment_version_2: v2 (2026-11-17): ADDITIONS ONLY. Protocol of v1 unchanged (v1 sha256 21cd630994b8a2c235d1c2aff31b9911bf0cd5135c9c9ef3360be421e752d658). Adds the measured results of the runs the protocol describes.

code.note: each arm ran from a `git archive eba66497` tree with these files laid over it; core resolved from source via a tsconfig path, so no build of the working tree was involved

measurement.artifacts_location: private run directories of the measuring session (row level carries ids and queries of a private vault); the hashes above identify them

results.rule_exemption_alone: after vs after-without-rule-exemption: 0 gains, 0 losses at R@1/3/10 and the same no-answer count — on this gold set the rule exemption moves nothing; the whole effect is the milder type-default factors
results.vs_replay_expectation: replay of 15.11.2026 expected R@3 257 and R@10 324; measured 253 and 321 on the production path. The replay used frozen candidate pools from another harness configuration; the before arm reproduces its 170 exactly

latency.what: applyStaleness over all 1631 notes as one pool, warm cache, ms per call, median of 7 x 100 calls, two rounds
latency.verdict: within the registered 5 % in both rounds (+2.4 % worst case)

results.longmemeval: functional identity by construction: longmemeval-run writes every session note as `type: reference` with no rulebook, valid_until or expires_after_days (longmemeval-run.ts writeQuestionVault), so neither branch of the policy can fire; no run needed

review_of_lifted_notes.population: 128 notes newly in some served top 3 after the switch (72 project-fact expired, 40 project-fact stale, 14 lesson stale, 1 workflow stale, 1 project-fact fresh); 2 carry superseded_by
review_of_lifted_notes.sample: the 50 lifted into the most top-3 lists
review_of_lifted_notes.by: an agent reading each note and searching the vault copy for newer notes on the same subject; not the owner
review_of_lifted_notes.pattern: the outdated ones are almost all dated snapshots: handovers, plans, release recipes and 'state of X' notes whose subject moved on; a newer note exists for most of them but is not linked as successor
review_of_lifted_notes.note: 16 of the 17 outdated notes are expected ids of gold cases, and 14 of them are among the 65 distinct targets of the 83 R@3 gains: part of the gain rewards finding an outdated snapshot because the gold label was written when the snapshot was current
